taken.mechanism: watch the new test fail, and for the predicted reason rather than an error, before writing the code
name the production change that should make a test fail before writing its body; a test with no nameable break has no job
derive expected values without the code under test or its helpers
a test that only intentional decisions can fail is a change detector; test the behaviour that depends on the decision
test the project's contract at its boundary, not the framework's own mechanics
before replacing a dependency, learn its side effects and keep the ones the test relies on real; doubles mirror the full real structure
test-only cleanup lives in test utilities, not on production classes
the realistic mutation kinds (wrong constant or argument, wrong branch, missing side effect, empty or default return, missing validation), turned here from a mental check into executed broken copies

rejected: deleting code written before its test: it conflicts with proportionality and the user's ownership of their code; westack keeps the code, proves the test with controls and labels the order test-after
the all-capitals iron law, rationalisation tables and red-flag lists: the westack rules carry the constraint with receipts instead of rhetoric
configuration as an exception to ask about: westack gives config a fitting check (check-only mode) instead
'every new function has a test' as a completion checkbox: a checkbox is a claim; coverage is not protection

taken.mechanism: vertical slices: one test, one minimal implementation, repeat, each a tracer bullet; writing all tests first is the anti-pattern
tests live at public seams; a test that breaks on a behaviour-preserving refactor is implementation-coupled, including checks through a back door
the tautological test: the expected value recomputed the way the code computes it passes by construction
doubles only at system boundaries; pass dependencies in; one function per external operation so each fake returns one shape

rejected: confirming every seam with the user before any test: kept only for bounded or cross-cutting work, with a recommended seam; a small slice just names its seam
refactoring outside the loop (left to review): the user's cycle keeps refactor-on-green inside each slice, under its own rerun
calling a separate codebase-design skill for vocabulary: the core's craft reference carries deep modules and seams

taken.mechanism: WB-05: Human gate written into the artifact: inline semi-automatic mode rewrites the approved text with a 'delete me to approve' marker, so the check fails until a person removes it.
WB-05: Deferred approval as a script: the reporter writes the move commands for every mismatch into a script instead of moving anything, so a person reviews the exact file list first.
WB-06: Each run logs every approved file it compared and every received-to-approved pair that differed, so a later step can find abandoned goldens or act on exactly the failed set.
WB-07: A scrubber must prove it fires: a custom date format is rejected unless its regex matches its own example, and lookup fails unless the example scrubs to the first token.
WB-07: Line-removal scrubber defect, found by reading: it deletes from the list it is looping over, so adjacent matching lines can survive. Scrubbers need cases with adjacent and repeated matches.

WB-08: Identity-preserving scrubbing: each distinct matched value gets a token numbered by first appearance (date0, date1), so equal values stay equal and different values stay different after scrubbing.

four modes with an honest order label: slice (test-first), regression (the pre-fix red counts as one control, plus one more), characterise (test-after, controls in place of red) and check-only (prose and config get a fitting check, never a fabricated red test)

helper_decision.reason: Two steps that agents get wrong by hand and that a script can check without trusting the agent: making broken copies (edited in the working tree and forgotten, a find text that silently did not apply so the 'control' equals the original, two 'distinct' copies that are the same, no hashes to show the copy differs) and judging control runs (a crash, an import error, zero tests or a different selection counted as a kill). The capability map had judged a helper unnecessary; the brief asked for a planner if justified, and these failure modes justify it. It runs nothing and calls no network; judge reuses the core's checks.py parser.
helper_decision.tests: tests/test_controls.py, 24 tests, written first: the red run against an interface-only stub failed 23 on assertions (the fixture self-check passed); then green 24 of 24.
helper_decision.controls: Four broken copies of controls.py made with its own plan command (branch, validation, boundary, constant). Three were killed on assertions with the same 24-test selection; one survivor (the zero-test guard) was argued equivalent because the core parser marks an empty parse incomplete and the selection check also blocks it, with three distinguishing inputs tried. An earlier round showed one copy killed only by a crash; the tests were strengthened to require a JSON refusal, after which it failed on an assertion.
